g.text: Receiver, Costas loop, and the two decision paths

One zero-IF quadrature demodulator does everything: its LO is a synthesizer on a VCXO, and the loop below steers the VCXO until the LO sits exactly on the far carrier. Then I is the data and Q the phase error. The FAST path (gain 4, 100 MHz) flags a bit in nanoseconds; the SLOW path (x20 more, 4.8 MHz) confirms or vetoes it 37 ns later from 11 dB further away. Levels are for the 10 m bench link (-53.9 dBm at the jack, DSA at 5.25 dB); sim/budget.py sections 2, 3, 6, 7, 7b.
puts the comparator floor near the noise
gain 5.8 dB into 450 Ω, IP1dB +11.6 dBm

g.text: VC: 0.3-3.0 V, 1.65 V centred, slow (3 kHz loop)
VC MON U.FL and the ADC watch it
VC_OFF (DAC) centres it; LOOP_SEL = FPGA makes a plain PLL on Q

text.style: fill: #444444; font: italic 6.5px 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle

path.style: fill: #eef7ee; stroke: #77aa77; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: Follow the red arrows left to right: 5.8 GHz comes in, gets amplified and levelled, and the demodulator multiplies it by the LO twice (once with the LO shifted 90°), giving I and Q at DC.
If the LO is exactly on the carrier, I is the carrier's amplitude (sign = the BPSK bit) and Q is zero; a phase error shows up in Q. The loop (orange) feeds sign(I)·Q, which is the phase error
with the BPSK ambiguity removed, through a PI filter to the VCXO; the synthesizer multiplies the VCXO by 232, so the LO follows. The loop is slow (3 kHz) on purpose: a 10 ns flip is far too
brief for it to notice, so the carrier phase reference survives the data. Every U.FL tap (12 of them) lets you look at a node on a scope: I MON, Q MON, ERR MON, VC MON, LO RX MON, REF OUT ...

path.style: fill: #fffbe6; stroke: #999988; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

fast latency jack-to-register: 14.2 ns PYNQ, 9.8 ns Icepi; slow confirm +37 ns
loop: f_n 3 kHz, ζ 0.7, pull ±580 kHz
